correctness.rationale: For \(C>0\), Bell-diagonal concurrence fixes the largest Bell eigenvalue to \((1+C)/2\). The other three probabilities map bijectively to absolute correlation coordinates \(r_i=C+2q_i\), giving the exact simplex slice \(r_i\ge C\), \(\sum r_i=1+2C\). Sorting reduces \(D_G\) to \((y^2+z^2)/4\) on a triangle. The minimum follows from \(y,z\ge C\); convexity places the maximum at a vertex; explicit evaluation yields the two candidate branches whose difference is \((1-C)(13C-1)/144\). The \(C=0\) separable octahedron is handled separately. Connectedness gives all intermediate values. Exact-rational replay confirms the algebra but is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The result supplies a complete and natural tradeoff diagram between a standard entanglement monotone and a historically important geometric correlation measure on the canonical Bell tetrahedron. The unexpected rank-three-to-Werner switch at \(C=1/13\) explains why the Werner line fails to maximize discord near separability and identifies every sharp boundary state, giving more structure than an isolated endpoint computation.
